$comment: PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATIONS for projection composition. Every expectation here was derived from docs/architecture/analytical-relation-doctrine.md — authority authored long before any combinator rule existed — and committed BEFORE the combinator rules were written. The implementation is tested against this file; this file is never edited to match the implementation. A disagreement is a finding about the algebra: report the previous representation's failure, justify any addition with a separating case, and add a NEW case that did not motivate it. The four refusal causes are the doctrine's own stage-3 declarations, not invented here.

doctrineBasis.states: layer is several atomic projections over ONE coordinate space with SHARED scales; layers declare scale sharing per channel; an unshared positional scale inside one coordinate space is the general form of the dual-axis illegality; annotations are relations layered in, and a target line has a unit and must be commensurable with the axis it sits on. facet repeats a projection over a partition with a declared scale policy (shared or free) per channel, and leaving the policy undeclared is ill-typed. embed is a projection as the value of a cell in a tabular projection, typed against the cell's channel budget. Admissibility is compositional: the legality of a composite is derived from the legality of its parts plus the combinator's rule, never from a whole-composite special case.

the diagnostic table declares exactly four stage-3 combinator causes: REL_UNIT_INCOMMENSURABLE_SHARED_SCALE (dimensional), REL_LAYER_SCALE_UNSHARED (declaration-missing), REL_FACET_SCALE_POLICY_UNDECLARED (declaration-missing), REL_EMBED_TASK_EXCEEDS_CHANNEL_BUDGET (task-invariant).

invariant 13 and falsification condition 8: a layered, faceted or embedded projection is admitted or rejected only by a rule written for that composite rather than derived from its parts and the combinator — the composite special case is a way the claim is falsified.

scopeDistinction.statement: A layer's shared scale is a relation WITHIN one coordinate space. A facet's scale policy is a relation ACROSS the panels a partition produces, each of which is its own coordinate space. The two therefore constrain different pairs of projections and are not flattened into one profile.
scopeDistinction.whyItIsRecorded: A single flattened sharing profile is the previous representation this slice rejected: it cannot express a facet whose panels each carry a shared-scale layer, and would refuse that composite. The separating case is U1 against U3.

cases.construction: Two retained programs over one cartesian coordinate space, both assigning position, measures commensurable by declared unit, sharing declares position shared.
cases.derivation: Doctrine line 160: a layer is several atomic projections over one coordinate space with shared scales, and layers declare scale sharing per channel. Every part is retained and the declared sharing is the one the combinator requires.

cases.construction: L1 with the sharing declaration absent entirely.
cases.derivation: Doctrine line 382: marks in one space imply one scale, so the declaration is REQUIRED and its absence is declaration-missing, not a default. Minimally changed neighbour of L1.

cases.construction: L1 with the second part's measure declaring a unit that shares no member with the first's units and appears in neither conversions list.
cases.derivation: Doctrine line 374 and line 160: dimensional analysis fails across a shared scale; the target line in the wrong unit is the doctrine's own second observation of this cause.

cases.construction: L1 with the second part's measure declaring no unit at all.
cases.derivation: A premise the declaration does not carry is UNPROVEN, not false — the same three-valued discipline the kernel applies to an unknown grain. The obligation name is the corpus's own `unit:commensurable`, already carried by FX_SALES_SUM_PERROW_UNIT_NO_ROWS and FX_H_INVENTORY_VALUE_UNKNOWN_UNIT. Refusing here would invent a contradiction the declaration does not state.

Doctrine line 160 names this exactly: an unshared positional scale inside one coordinate space is the general form of the dual-axis illegality. Same cause as L2 because it is one cause observed twice.

cases.construction: Two retained programs, a declared partition over the result-grain dimension, policy declares position shared.
cases.derivation: Doctrine line 161: facet repeats a projection over a partition with a declared scale policy per channel. Shared is a legal policy and it asserts cross-panel comparability.

cases.construction: F1 with the policy absent entirely.
cases.derivation: Doctrine line 383 and line 161: leaving the policy undeclared is ill-typed. Minimally changed neighbour of F1.

Doctrine line 161: free scales trade comparability for resolution and that trade is a CLAIM, so it is legal and it differs from F1 by exactly the claim it names. Every other claim is unchanged, which is what makes the pair separating.

cases.construction: A tabular host projection whose cell budget carries position and text; the embedded part declares the trend task.
cases.derivation: Doctrine line 162: with position only and no baseline or axis the embedded projection can serve a trend task. Text additionally makes the value recoverable.

cases.construction: E1 with the embedded part declaring magnitude-comparison instead of trend.
cases.derivation: Doctrine lines 162 and 405: the embedded projection is typed against the cell's channel budget and CANNOT serve a magnitude comparison there, because the budget carries no baseline or axis. Minimally changed neighbour of E1.

cases.construction: L1 with exactly one part replaced by an otherwise identical program whose operation the analytical rules refuse.
cases.derivation: Doctrine lines 164 and 261 plus falsification condition 8: the composite is refused because a PART is refused, and it carries that part's own cause verbatim. A composite-specific cause here would mean the composite is being judged by something other than its parts.

cases.construction: A layer over [a facet whose policy declares position free, a single-row annotation part], sharing position shared.
cases.derivation: Nested rule interaction. The facet exposes its panels as separately scaled, so the outer layer has no single position scale to share and cannot be one coordinate space. Neither combinator's rule was written for this pairing; the contradiction is read off the operand's exposed profile.

cases.construction: A facet over [a layer over two retained programs sharing position], policy declares position free.
cases.derivation: UNFAMILIAR RECOMBINATION, expected outcome fixed before the implementation. The inner layer shares one scale WITHIN each panel; the outer facet declines to share it ACROSS panels. Each panel is its own coordinate space, so the layer's requirement is satisfied and the facet's free policy is a legal trade made once per panel. There is no contradiction, so the composite is RETAINED, with cross-panel comparability withheld. A representation that flattens the two scopes into one profile refuses this and is wrong.

cases.construction: U1 with the facet policy declaring position shared.
cases.derivation: The materially different policy variant. Same construction and same inner layer; the policy is the only difference, so the outcome must differ by exactly the claim the policy names and by nothing else.

cases.construction: U1 with the inner layer's sharing declaration absent.
cases.derivation: The unfamiliar construction is judged from its PARTS. The fault is the inner layer's own missing declaration, so the cause is the layer's and not a facet cause — which is how we know no rule was written for facets-of-layers.

cases.construction: L1 with an additional sharing declaration for a channel no part assigns.
cases.derivation: Invariant-preserving perturbation. No part reads that channel, so no scale is shared over it and the declaration constrains nothing. Verdict and induced claims must be identical to L1.

cases.construction: F1 with an additional policy entry for a channel no part assigns.
cases.derivation: Invariant-preserving perturbation, the facet counterpart: a policy for a channel the projection does not read is inert, so the undeclared-policy refusal must not fire on it and no claim may move.

corpusFinding.statement: No committed relation fixture in analytical-fixtures declares a unit on any field, so over the committed corpus every layer's shared-channel commensurability is UNPROVEN and the dimensional refusal is reachable only over an authored declaration.
corpusFinding.measuredBy: grep for a field-level unit across the committed fixture structures
corpusFinding.consequence: L3 is exercised over an authored structure, and L4 is what the corpus itself produces. Neither branch is presented as the other.

nonClaims: The four causes are the doctrine's stage-3 declarations; this slice implements four of them and asserts nothing about the others.
A retained composite's claim set is derived from its parts and its declarations within the claim vocabulary this layer owns; it is not a proof that the vocabulary is complete.
The cell channel budget is declared, not measured: `embed` types the embedded part against the budget the declaration carries and asserts nothing about what a real cell renders.
Only the layer, facet and embed combinators named by the doctrine are typed here; no other composition operator is claimed.
